title: Consolidated results of the nine-lane landscape-first investigation
interpretation_rule: Novelty below means new within this programme unless explicitly promoted by a literature audit and expert review; it is not a priority claim.

lanes.name: Measurement-first inverse reconstruction
lanes.established_landscape: Congruence classification of positive matrices, generalized eigenvalues and simultaneous response tomography are standard linear algebra and inverse-problem tools.
lanes.programme_result: One SPD two-port response carries no GL2 calibration invariant; two responses carry a generalized spectrum; three can carry a noncommutativity magnitude, while orientation still needs a physical handedness convention.
lanes.generic_universality: The invariants apply to any calibrated positive two-port system and are not Standard-Model-specific.
lanes.novelty_status: Potentially useful programme-specific synthesis and experimental hierarchy; no external priority claim.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Measure two or three explicitly defined gauge-invariant source protocols on the same calibrated apparatus and test invariance under every allowed source-frame recalibration.
lanes.go_signal: A dimensionless invariant tracks the independent topology assignment with no refit.
lanes.no_go_signal: The relation changes under an allowed calibration or is insensitive to topology.

lanes.name: RG and OPE operator closure
lanes.established_landscape: Noether-current quotients, anomaly constraints, spurion breaking and anomalous-dimension mixing are standard quantum-field-theory machinery.
lanes.programme_result: The complete gauge-typed direct-current problem reduces exactly to five physical coordinates: four Yukawa-breaking differences and one independent anomaly coordinate. Hypercharge/EOM and B-L null directions do not enlarge this quotient. The shared-field metric has four distinct eigenvalues and neither incidence convention is an eigenray, so exact incidence/B-L two-current closure fails at leading noncontact order. The incidence family retains the non-generic benchmark relation A2=A3=vu+vd, while its normalization fork remains visible in the charged-lepton coordinate.
lanes.generic_universality: The B-L result is established Standard-Model structure; the nonclosure determinant is specific to the programme's declared incidence vector and chosen minimal spurion form.
lanes.novelty_status: The direct vector-source anomalous-dimension matrix remains uncomputed. Established full ALP RGE and matching have been executed, but the exact incidence charge ray is not independently derived. The absorptive metric is top-dominated and the completed canonical middle-slot metric matches neither incidence convention. A potentially new result therefore requires an action-derived selector or a deliberately restricted benchmark test.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Construct bottom- and weak-anomaly-sensitive observables with interference information: together with top production and charged-lepton lifetime they give visible rank four and test the signed incidence residual; the neutrino coordinate remains practically inaccessible at low mass.
lanes.go_signal: A source-derived metric uniquely fixes the relative incidence ray, production-plus-lifetime data distinguish its accessible coordinates after nuisance profiling, or the direct vector module develops a stable quotient.
lanes.no_go_signal: No physical construction selects an incidence normalization, ordinary ALP nuisance directions reproduce the accessible correlations, and the direct source frame remains scheme-dependent.

lanes.name: Nonperturbative lattice and functional response
lanes.established_landscape: Domain-wall and overlap methods, lattice refinement, projected resolvents and spectral positivity are established regulator tools for chiral fermions.
lanes.programme_result: The exact wall zero pole, rank-one residue and Herglotz positivity survive refinement, but the limiting two-probe eigenvector depends continuously on wall decay lengths and probe placement.
lanes.generic_universality: Index protection and projected-resolvent positivity are generic; the equal-face ray follows from imposed reflection symmetry rather than the Standard Model.
lanes.novelty_status: New-to-programme refinement benchmark; not a new lattice-fermion theorem.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Simulate gauge-invariant current correlators with domain-wall or overlap fermions and jointly extrapolate Ward residuals, mirror contamination and eigenframe drift.
lanes.go_signal: A normalized relation survives regulator, volume, profile and smearing changes.
lanes.no_go_signal: Only pole rank and positivity survive while the frame follows adjustable regulator preparation.

lanes.name: Boundary theory and anomaly inflow
lanes.established_landscape: Domain-wall chirality, anomaly inflow and helicity reversal under wall-normal reversal are established boundary-field-theory effects.
lanes.programme_result: Wall reversal flips the helicity-resolved pole but leaves the spin-summed H2(R) face response even, proving that chirality does not automatically transmit orientation to the programme's two-face carrier.
lanes.generic_universality: The even spin trace and odd helicity trace are generic Pauli/Weyl algebra facts.
lanes.novelty_status: A sharp programme-specific bridge obstruction and experimental discriminator; not a new anomaly-inflow theorem.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Introduce the smallest gauge-invariant spin-face or spin-internal coupling and test whether wall reversal changes the face response without arbitrary counterterms.
lanes.go_signal: The same bulk datum fixes chirality and a measured face-orientation witness.
lanes.no_go_signal: The face orientation requires an independent boundary coupling or convention.

lanes.name: Spectral triples and graded superconnections
lanes.established_landscape: Finite real spectral triples encode matter as bimodules; Krajewski diagrams classify compatible representations and Dirac links; right-handed-neutrino Majorana terms create known orientability tension.
lanes.programme_result: Gauge dressing identifies the three extra doubled-Furey links as S1 and optional S3 scalar-leptoquark channels. Crossing with the exceptional Spin(10) ten gives nine component channels: four ordinary Yukawas, precisely the three Furey S1 links and two diquark links. The Furey first-order intersection is exactly the proton-safer seven-channel subset; full Spin(10) covariance restores the two diquark partners, so doublet-triplet splitting or another breaking mechanism is unavoidable.
lanes.generic_universality: The obstruction is a general property of diagonal left and right actions on distinct points, not special to Furey matter.
lanes.novelty_status: The exact programme-specific seven-link count and neutral-endpoint quotient obstruction are new within the programme. Krajewski diagrams and the general Majorana-orientability tension are established; full gauge dressing is still required before claiming a coefficient reduction.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Construct an explicit broken exceptional/Furey action and test whether it removes the Q-Q and uc-dc diquark channels without arbitrary zeros while retaining the four Yukawas and, optionally, the proton-safer S1 subset.
lanes.go_signal: One common algebra/action derives colour-linearity and the four observed Yukawa links, or predicts a sharply constrained leptoquark sector with its basic diquark partners absent.
lanes.no_go_signal: Colour-linearity and Majorana structure remain independent manual restrictions on otherwise arbitrary finite-Dirac data.

lanes.name: Amplitudes and bootstrap constraints
lanes.established_landscape: Projective cross-ratios, form-factor decomposition, dispersion relations and positivity bounds are standard on-shell and S-matrix tools.
lanes.programme_result: Positive-energy absorptive response supplies a contact- and EOM-insensitive Yukawa metric. In the ALP realization, production times proper decay length cancels the common scale and discriminates restricted charge patterns. The exact five-coordinate observable audit shows that top, bottom, charged-lepton and genuinely weak-anomaly rows give visible rank four, sufficient to test the incidence residual and charged-lepton normalization. A neutrino-chirality row would give rank five but is practically invisible at low mass; present Upsilon sensitivity is about 2190 times too weak for the required bottom compass.
lanes.generic_universality: Cross-ratio invariance is generic projective geometry; the numerical value is bookkeeping from the input charges, not a new prediction.
lanes.novelty_status: A concrete normalization-free phenomenological correlation and an explicit identifiability boundary now exist, calculated with established ALP machinery. Near-term novelty is limited to testing restricted UV rays; a claim to reconstruct the complete incidence vector would exceed present experimental information.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Build a reduced-rank likelihood combining top-sensitive rare-meson production, charged-lepton lifetime, a bottom compass and a genuinely electroweak weak-anomaly observable, including interference information for the sign of the incidence residual.
lanes.go_signal: The rank-four visible system separates restricted incidence-family rays and tests the signed relation A2=vu+vd after independent electroweak gauge coefficients are profiled.
lanes.no_go_signal: No viable bottom or weak-anomaly compass exists, or rate and nuisance degeneracies continuously reproduce the incidence relation.

lanes.name: Modular and operator-algebraic reconstruction
lanes.established_landscape: Finite standard forms, modular operators and Bloch-ball/unitary geometry are established operator theory.
lanes.programme_result: One faithful M2 state supplies modular flow but neither H2(R) nor orientation. An ordered nonparallel pair canonically selects a real plane, and a third noncoplanar state supplies the unitary-invariant pseudoscalar tau=r0 dot (r1 cross r2).
lanes.generic_universality: The construction applies to every qubit or two-channel density-matrix family and is not uniquely modular-QFT or Standard-Model structure.
lanes.novelty_status: The three-state orientation theorem is directly overlapped by 2026 qubit-multistate Bargmann work; only the response-calibration boundary and programme application remain specific.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Specify three physically ordered preparations, determine their true equivalence group and compare the sign of tau with an independently reversed topology witness.
lanes.go_signal: The state family and inclusion canonically fix the selector and reversal under all physically allowed recalibrations.
lanes.no_go_signal: Ordering is conventional, states are coplanar or general calibration changes the sign.

lanes.name: Defect and topological response
lanes.established_landscape: Toeplitz indices, class-D parity, real eigenbundles and Stiefel-Whitney classes are established topological tools; strict matrix-Herglotz domains forbid interior determinant zeros.
lanes.programme_result: A strictly positive H2(R) defect loop can have an odd Mobius principal eigenline while its determinant winding remains zero. An isotropic passive frequency extension carries the same parity but creates no genuine two-dimensional mixed class.
lanes.generic_universality: The Mobius eigenline occurs in arbitrary reciprocal two-port families with a maintained eigenvalue gap.
lanes.novelty_status: The real-eigenline topology is established Stiefel-Whitney physics; the positive-response obstruction and programme application are specific, but no physical defect is derived.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Transport a signed response eigenmode around a field-generated defect and test its sign holonomy and correlation with the topology orientation.
lanes.go_signal: A derived defect realizes the parity robustly and fixes its physical port interpretation.
lanes.no_go_signal: The effect is a freely engineered reciprocal two-port twist or vanishes on the complete domain.

lanes.name: Emergent and analogue response
lanes.established_landscape: Schur complements, passive mechanical admittance and hidden-mode tomography are standard network and control theory.
lanes.programme_result: A three-oscillator passive network has two reversed coupling graphs with identical static H2(R) response but an exactly sign-reversing dynamic witness G11-G22.
lanes.generic_universality: The complete carrier-plus-orientation pattern is realizable by elementary springs and masses.
lanes.novelty_status: Concrete programme testbed and decisive universality warning; not evidence for fundamental ontology.
lanes.next_decision_experiment: Build the three-resonator device and use it to validate the calibration, reversal and eigenline protocols proposed by L1, L7 and L8.
lanes.go_signal: The analogue discriminates hidden orientations dynamically and calibrates the proposed observables.
lanes.no_go_signal: A fundamental claim relies only on phenomena already reproduced by this generic network.

continuation_results.result: Local RG fixes incidence factorization and its kernel, but a displayed running eigenframe is scheme-dependent.
The absorptive spectral matrix supplies a physical fixed-energy broken-current metric.
The spectral leading direction is a tau-bottom-top threshold staircase rather than a universal axis.
Derivative pseudoscalar coupling identifies the quotient with ALP EFT and leaves only Y and B-L jointly null.
The incidence ALP ray runs away from itself under published top-Yukawa evolution.
Universal UV charges generate a rank-one CKM flavor projector through top-Yukawa running.
Full ALP running makes third-family-only versus universal embeddings phenomenologically decisive.
Production times lifetime cancels the overall ALP scale and distinguishes the relative incidence charge pattern from two same-top-coupling comparators.
Vector-path extraction of the published NA62 curve revises the 100 MeV characteristic crossings to 6.5e7 and 7.3e8 GeV while preserving order-of-magnitude embedding separation.
At 300 MeV the published dimuon acceptance converts the production-lifetime correlation into curve crossings separated from 1.08e6 to 3.39e6 GeV across same-top-coupling charge patterns.
Eight UV coefficients reduce to five physical low-energy coordinates, while realistic production and lifetime measurements practically resolve only three or four directions.
The Furey incidence calculation robustly fixes the sterile-neutrino kernel but two natural response contractions give distinct charged-lepton coefficients and ALP rays.
Radiative Upsilon decay supplies the missing bottom-sensitive coordinate, but present invisible limits are about 2190 times above the incidence prediction at the reference point.

The next checkpoint separates algebraic selection of the incidence metric, experimental readout of a reduced top-lepton slice, the missing bottom compass and the independent direct-current mixing problem.
The completed basis-independent middle-slot frame has weights (14,14,8,2,6,12) and no kernel, so it selects neither completed incidence normalization.
The simplest action-derived completed-fermion metric is full rank and cannot generate the sterile kernel, but it canonically removes physically invisible B-L shear from the incidence plane.
Physical-source, exceptional-representation and doubled-spectral-geometry calculations independently organize the candidate carrier but each leaves a precisely identified selector freedom.
The exact direct-current quotient has five physical coordinates and neither incidence convention is an eigenray, although both retain one non-generic anomaly relation.

Round two reduces the three trunks to a five-coordinate current quotient, an invariantly selected exceptional rank-one orbit with spontaneous face choice, and a colour-linearity fork between Standard-Model Yukawas and optional S1/S3 leptoquarks.
Top, bottom, charged-lepton and weak-anomaly rows give visible rank four and test the incidence residual; the fifth neutrino-chirality coordinate is practically inaccessible in the low-mass regime.

Cross-branch closure identifies a rank-four visible experiment, a healthy exceptional Morse-Bott selector whose tangent 16 is bosonic, and an exact two-diquark incompatibility between Spin(10) covariance and Furey first order.

paper_clusters.title: Calibration, state frames and topology in passive two-channel response
paper_clusters.core: A hierarchy from one response with no calibration invariant, through two-state frame selection, to three-state orientation and Mobius defect holonomy, with a three-oscillator falsification platform.

paper_clusters.title: The Standard-Model current plane under Yukawa breaking and on-shell calibration
paper_clusters.core: Classical current quotient, anomaly-safe axis, local-RG scheme boundary, ALP completion, full running, incidence-normalization fork and a scale-free top-lepton discriminator with a quantified missing bottom direction.

paper_clusters.title: Boundary chirality does not automatically orient a two-face response
paper_clusters.core: Wall helicity is orientation-odd while spin-summed face response is even; refinement preserves the pole but leaves its ray profile-dependent.

paper_clusters.title: Furey TROs versus finite spectral geometry
paper_clusters.core: The naive point model fails first order, making a full arrow/Krajewski classification the correct next problem.

overall_verdict: The expansion now has three convergent reductions and three concrete bottlenecks. The direct-current and ALP descriptions independently reach a five-coordinate quotient whose visible experimental map has rank four, requiring bottom, weak-anomaly and interference information. The exceptional rank-one potential is a healthy Morse-Bott selector, but its tangent 16 consists of scalar Goldstone directions rather than the fermionic generation. The exceptional ten reproduces the Furey S1 links only by restoring two proton-dangerous diquark partners excluded by Furey first order. However, no lane presently derives one common broken action that supplies the fermion bundle, removes those diquark channels without arbitrary zeros and maps the five source coordinates to normalized observables or Spin(2,3) orientation.
